The measured b_i is the threshold shift when the neighbor flips: Δγ_threshold for rotor i = −Δτ_i^{coupling}/k_d L (dividing by drive torque sensitivity k_d L). And Δτ_i^{coupling} when σ_j flips = the change in coupling torque on i as θ_j goes from −θ_j^stop to +θ_j^stop. ∂τ_i/∂θ_j = k_c (∂R/∂θ_i)(∂R/∂θ_j) + k_c(R−ℓ0)∂²R/∂θ_i∂θ_j. b_i = −(1/(k_d L cosθ...)) * Δτ_i where Δτ_i = K_ij * (θ_j^+ − θ_j^-) = K_ij * 2θ_j^stop (for small stop angles), where K_ij = k_c (∂R/∂θ_i)(∂R/∂θ_j) evaluated... Hmm, ∂R/∂θ_j ≈ ℓ_j * something. So K_ij ∝ k_c ℓ_i ℓ_j × geometry factor. Then b_i = 2θ_j^stop * K_ij/(k_d L).

This is exchange-coupled field: b_i ∝ (motion amplitude of j).

Now, where can I add genuinely new conceptual content? My own strongest asset: the mechanically derived relation between K_ij and measurable geometry: K_ij = k_c (∂R/∂θ_i)(∂R/∂θ_j) — a rank-one, positive-semidefinite structure! That's a big deal: because the exchange coupling from a single spring is a product of moment arms, K_ij = k_c a_i a_j where a_i = ∂R/∂θ_i (moment arm). This means K is a rank-one matrix, always "ferromagnetic" in the sense K_ij > 0 up to signs of a_i (i.e., the metric!). The sign of K_ij is determined by the relative orientation of the two moment arms (i.e., which side of the pivot the spring attaches, sign convention of θ). And any sign flip is a gauge (relabeling), so a single-spring coupling can never produce frustration! Frustration requires either multiple springs (a sum of rank-one terms with different metrics, i.e., different assignment of a_i signs) or a spring whose rest-length term (R−ℓ0) contributes via ∂²R/∂θ_i∂θ_j.

That's a concrete, checkable claim: For a single linear spring between two rotors, the coupling energy is U = ½k_c(R(θ_i,θ_j)−ℓ0)², so the Hessian is k_c ∂_iR ∂_jR + k_c(R−ℓ0)∂_i∂_jR. At the "exchange" level the first term is rank-one; the second term (prestress) is not necessarily rank-one and can change signs — and can be negative (compressed spring, R<ℓ0). So frustration (sign product −1 around a loop) requires either prestress/second-order geometric terms or more than one spring per edge with crossing attachments. That connects directly to the wiring parity (parallel vs crossed) hypothesis: parallel/crossed is a statement about the relative signs of a_i and a_j, i.e., exactly the gauge. Since gauge doesn't matter for parity, the parallel vs crossed distinction cannot generate frustration by itself — only the sign of the product around a loop, which is gauge-invariant, and for rank-one couplings signs can be gauged away on a tree; on loops the product of a_i a_j around a cycle = product of squares = +1 times (sign of k_c): always balanced. So: a network of single linear springs, one per edge, with no prestress, is never frustrated. Frustration needs either ≥2 springs with incommensurate gauges... hmm actually with 2 springs: K_ij = k_c1 a_i^(1)a_j^(1) + k_c2 a_i^(2)a_j^(2). Sign can be anything, e.g., if spring 1 attaches with a_i>0,a_j>0 and spring 2 with a_i>0,a_j<0, then K_ij = k_c1 a b − k_c2 a c <0. So frustration in a loop requires heterogeneous attachment geometry. Since pair_A is "parallel coupling springs" (two springs per edge) and pair_B "crossed", the difference in b sign is exactly the competition between the two rank-one terms! That's a real refinement: the sign is set by which of the two parallel springs dominates (or by the crossing geometry). And it means |b| can be tuned continuously through zero by making the two springs' contributions cancel — a "sign knob" the peer's sign(K)=−sign(b) reading doesn't have. That's a nice conditional consequence: near the sign-change point, |b|→0 and the edge's field channel vanishes; parity becomes ill-defined/continuously tunable. That's a genuinely useful conceptual move: sign of an edge is not a discrete wiring fact but the sign of a sum of rank-one terms; hence "gauge" is local, and frustration is a property of the sum-structure.

FOCUS: The clamped table's neighbor dependence is a *linear-response coefficient* (per radian), λ_ij = b_i/(2θ_j^stop) — and mechanically λ_ij = ∂²U/∂θ_i∂θ_j /(k_d L) = [k_c a_i a_j + k_c(R−ℓ0)∂_i∂_j R]/(k_d L). Two consequences:

(2) Rank-one structure: for a single spring, the leading term is k_c a_i a_j, a *product* of moment arms. Consequence: |λ| can be tuned through zero by making the two springs' contributions cancel — near that point the field channel vanishes while the stiffness channel (sum of k_c a_i², always positive) does NOT vanish. So the two channels can be separated by a *sign-knob*: you can null the field (parity content) while keeping the width shrink.
